usage: contract [-h]
                {returns-none,returns-zero,returns-false,returns-empty-string,returns-list,returns-tuple,returns-dict,returns-set,returns-generator,returns-iterator,streams-then-fails,raises-command-error,raises-command-error-coded,raises-system-exit-code,raises-system-exit-message}
                ...

The D2 contract rows, one command each.

positional arguments:
  {returns-none,returns-zero,returns-false,returns-empty-string,returns-list,returns-tuple,returns-dict,returns-set,returns-generator,returns-iterator,streams-then-fails,raises-command-error,raises-command-error-coded,raises-system-exit-code,raises-system-exit-message}
    returns-none        Row 17: None prints NOTHING -- not 'None', not a blank line.
    returns-zero        Row 17: 0 DOES print, which is why the check cannot be `if result:`.
    returns-false       Row 17: False DOES print.
    returns-empty-string
                        Row 17: '' DOES print -- as a blank line.
    returns-list        Row 16: a list iterates, one line per item.
    returns-tuple       Row 16: a tuple iterates too.
    returns-dict        Row 16: a dict is NOT iterated. It prints its repr, on one line.
    returns-set         Row 16: a set is not in the whitelist either, so it prints its repr. Set
                        repr ordering is stable here only because the set has one element -- which
                        is the point: the corpus may not depend on hash ordering.
    returns-generator   Row 16: a generator IS in the whitelist, and iterates.
    returns-iterator    Row 16, the trap: `iter([...])` is a `list_iterator`, NOT a GeneratorType.
                        The whitelist is three concrete types, so this prints a repr, not two
                        lines. Any fleet command returning `map(...)`, `filter(...)` or a
                        comprehension-fed iterator is printing a repr today.
    streams-then-fails  Row 18: a generator streams LAZILY, so what it yielded lands before the
                        error.
    raises-command-error
                        Row 19: `CommandError` is one line on stderr and a non-zero exit, no
                        traceback.
    raises-command-error-coded
                        Row 19: and it carries its own exit code, which is NOT 1.
    raises-system-exit-code
                        Row 19: a SystemExit keeps its exit code.
    raises-system-exit-message
                        Row 19: a SystemExit with a string prints it and exits 1.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

note: Recorded in-process from real argh against cw/tests/fixtures.py. argh is not a dependency of cw; see misc/record_goldens.py.
pins: The egress and error rows, which every repo shape has in it but none exercises on purpose: the three-concrete-type whitelist (a dict prints on ONE line and a plain iterator prints a repr), None printing nothing while 0/False/'' print, lazy generator streaming, and CommandError's one-line stderr and exit code.
